newsitem.title: DUBAI: Gulf LPG weak on summer demand lull - trade.
newsitem.headline: Gulf LPG weak on summer demand lull - trade.

text.p: Gulf propane and butane spot cargoes have extended their price discounts to Saudi Aramco's benchmark LPG contract price (CP) because of a sharp seasonal drop-off in Asian demand, Gulf traders said on Wednesday.
Propane was talked at around $8-15 a tonne discount to the Aramco August CP of $175, versus parity early last month.
Butane, better supported by Indian demand, talked at a $5-10 a tonne discount to the July CP of $192.
"Propane will stay weak until winter stock-building begins again in late August and September," said one trader.
LPG prices traditionally rally from the fourth quarter and peak in January and February as heating demand increases.
Gulf propane prices hit as high as $345 in January 1997.

Gulf traders expected Aramco at the end of this month to keep its CP for August liftings unchanged or carry out a modest price discount of $5-10 after one of its regular monthly propane tenders was awarded at $170-175.
Aramco's CP is a widely-used benchmark for some 10 million tonnes a year of LPG exports from Kuwait, United Arab Emirates, Iran and Qatar.
Aramco exports an additional 14 million tonnes a year of LPG, making it the world's largest exporter of the fuel.
